item.title: HKFP Lens: Crowds flock to see Kam Tin’s once-in-a-decade Jiao Festival
item.description: The once-in-a-decade Jiao Festival in Kam Tin – which features a massive centrepiece that entered the Guinness World Records as the world’s largest temporary bamboo altar – has drawn to a successful close. item.title: Taiwan lodges WTO complaint over Canadian steel tariffs
item.description: Taiwan has launched a complaint with the World Trade Organization over Canadian tariffs slapped on imports of steel goods, the global trade body said Thursday. WTO said that Taiwan, which is known as Chinese Taipei within the organisation, had requested that it initiate “dispute consultations with Canada”, charging it was breaching international trade rules. item.title: After deadly Tai Po fire, Hong Kong’s urban redevelopment body has no room for complacency
item.description: The deadly Wang Fuk Court fire has put a spotlight on the maintenance of ageing buildings in Hong Kong. Whether in news reports, commentaries, or daily banters, nearly all discussions are either about the mandatory building renovation scheme, bid-rigging, or ways to stamp out bid-rigging. item.title: Tai Po fire: Domestic workers pick up the pieces amid emotional trauma, job loss
item.description: In the aftermath of Hong Kong’s biggest fire in decades, Filipina domestic worker Vame Verador lost more than just her abode and most prized possessions. item.title: Jimmy Lai, the Hong Kong media ‘troublemaker’ in Beijing’s crosshairs
item.description: A rags-to-riches tycoon, Hong Kong media boss Jimmy Lai is a self-styled “troublemaker” who has long been a thorn in Beijing’s side with his caustic tabloids and unapologetic support for democracy.
